Cohesive

/kō-HĒ-siv/ — rhymes with adhesive · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Something cohesive holds together as a single, well-connected whole, with each part fitting logically with the others.

After a season together, the once-scattered players became a cohesive team.

Worked Example

The author's essay was cohesive, with each paragraph flowing naturally into the next and all ideas linking back to the central thesis.

Cohesive is more precise than 'organized' or 'well-written' because it captures the specific quality that parts bond together and fit logically, not just that they are arranged neatly.

How Cohesive Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

unified

unified: joined together into one single whole

integrated

integrated: with parts combined smoothly into one

seamless

seamless: flowing together with no visible joins

Antonyms

fragmented

fragmented: broken into disconnected, separate little pieces

disjointed

disjointed: with parts that fail to connect

How Strong Is It? — scattered → organized → cohesive → unified

scattered vs. cohesive

scattered vs. cohesive: Scattered sits at the very bottom of this scale — it is the opposite of cohesive, describing pieces flung apart with no connection at all.

organized vs. cohesive

organized vs. cohesive: Organized is stronger than scattered but weaker than cohesive: organized parts are neatly arranged, while cohesive parts actually hold together and support one another as a whole.

unified vs. cohesive

unified vs. cohesive: Unified is even stronger than cohesive — a cohesive group's parts fit tightly together, but a unified group has fused so completely that it acts as a single thing.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — co- (com-)

Prefix — co- (com-): together (Latin)

Root — hes

Root — hes: to stick, cling (Latin)

Suffix — -ive

Suffix — -ive: adjective-forming: tending to (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Co- ('together') + hes ('to stick') + -ive ('tending to') describes something that tends to stick together — a cohesive team or essay is one whose parts hold firmly to each other as a single whole.

Use the root in a new word: adhesive

Use the root in a new word: adhesive: The adhesive on the tape makes it stick firmly to the wall — it shares the Latin root haerere, 'to stick,' with cohesive, which describes parts sticking together as one whole.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / academic

Cohesive describes a quality where all parts fit together logically and feel bonded as a whole. Use it for teams, essays, plots, or arguments. For simply well-organized work, 'organized' is often simpler; for smooth surfaces, 'seamless' is better.
